blocks.text: Non-ALR Rural Estates vs ALR Country Acreages in Abbotsford

parts.t: Buyers searching for an acreage in Abbotsford—a home on 1 to 20+ acres with privacy, space for a detached workshop, RV/truck parking, or hobby farming—encounter two fundamentally different land-use regimes: Non-ALR Rural Residential Acreages and Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) Acreages. Knowing which category an address falls into is the single most important first step before touring.

Non-ALR rural residential acreages (typically zoned RR2 or RR3 under Abbotsford Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014) are concentrated on the forested slopes of Sumas Mountain and Straiton in northeast Abbotsford, along with select rural pockets in Bradner and Aberdeen. Because these parcels sit outside the ALR, they are not bound by provincial Agricultural Land Commission house floor-area caps or farm-use covenants. By contrast, rolling 2 to 10 acre parcels across Bradner, Aberdeen, Matsqui, South Poplar, and Sumas Prairie mostly sit inside the ALR (A1 or A2 zoning), offering gentle pasture or berry topography and potential BC Assessment Farm Class property tax savings if leased or farmed.

blocks.text: Wells, Septic Systems, Workshops, and Second Residences

parts.t: Most Abbotsford acreages outside the urban boundary rely on a private drilled water well and an onsite septic system rather than municipal water and sanitary sewer. During your subject period, always complete a professional well flow-rate test (gallons per minute recovery) and a comprehensive bacteria/metals/nitrates lab water quality test, alongside a Type 1 or Type 2 septic inspection and tank pump-out. If you plan to build an outbuilding, coach house, or 40x60 shop, check the parcel's lot coverage limits, Streamside Protection (riparian creek) setbacks, Steep Slope or Floodplain Development Permit Area overlays, and ALC additional-residence rules.

blocks.text: 7 Common Questions About Abbotsford Acreages for Sale

parts.t: Where are the best areas in Abbotsford to buy a 1 to 10 acre property?

Top acreage areas include Sumas Mountain / Straiton (forested hillside estates, many outside the ALR), Bradner and Aberdeen on the west side (rolling country acreages with quick Highway 1 access), Matsqui along the northern ridge and prairie, and South Poplar.
How do I know if an Abbotsford acreage is inside or outside the ALR?

Check the exact parcel on the BC Agricultural Land Commission map and the City of Abbotsford webmap. Properties zoned A1 or A2 are inside the ALR, whereas properties zoned RR2 or RR3 (common on Sumas Mountain) are generally outside the ALR.
Can I have a second house or detached guest suite on an Abbotsford acreage?

On ALR land, provincial and municipal rules generally permit one additional small residence up to 90 sq m (968 sq ft) subject to zoning, servicing, and setbacks. On non-ALR Rural Residential lots, secondary suite and accessory building rules are governed by City of Abbotsford Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014.
What water and sewer inspections are needed when buying an Abbotsford acreage?

Unless the parcel is connected to a municipal water line, you should always include contract subjects for a well flow-rate test, a certified laboratory potability water test, and a professional septic system inspection.
Can I park commercial trucks or run a home business on an Abbotsford acreage?

Commercial vehicle parking and home-occupation uses depend strictly on whether the property is in the ALR (where non-farm commercial trucking or contractor yards are heavily restricted by the ALC) or on non-ALR rural land. Always verify permitted uses with the City of Abbotsford before offering.
How is an acreage different from a commercial farm listing?

Acreage buyers focus primarily on the residence, shop, privacy, and 1 to 10 acres of land (including hobby farms), whereas our Abbotsford Farms and Poultry Farms pages also cover large commercial agricultural operations up to 160+ acres.
